title: Open direct image under reduction of the ambient scheme
statement: Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion, def-pc-scheme]. Let $r:X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ and $s:U_{\mathrm{red}}\to U$ be their reductions [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], and let $j_{\mathrm{red}}:U_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X_{\mathrm{red}}$ be the induced open immersion. For any commutative ring $\Lambda$ and any sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $U$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], there is a $\Lambda$-linear isomorphism, natural in $F$, $$j_*F\ \cong\ r_*j_{\mathrm{red},*}s^{-1}F.$$ Here direct and inverse image are those of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] for constant coefficient rings. No reducedness, Noetherianity, finiteness or constructibility assumption on $X$, $\Lambda$ or $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph, reduction comparison before Noetherian induction

proof.text: The induced reduction square commutes: $r\circ j_{\mathrm{red}}=j\circ s$. Indeed, identify $U$ with its open image using [def-weil-open-immersion]. The nilradical sheaf of $U$ is the restriction of that of $X$: on every affine open $V\subseteq U$, both are the nilradical of the same ring $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_U)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$. The quotient maps defining reduction in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] therefore restrict to one another. Thus $j_{\mathrm{red}}$ is the inclusion of the corresponding open in $X_{\mathrm{red}}$, and both composites have the same underlying inclusion and the same map of structure sheaves.

source.place: First paragraph: reduction comparison; Schemes Tag 01J4 (schemes-definition-reduced-induced-scheme)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] applied to the arbitrary scheme $U$, its reduction $s:U_{\mathrm{red}}\to U$ is a universal homeomorphism. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] to $s$: the inverse and direct images on the small etale topoi are quasi-inverse, so the adjunction unit on the underlying abelian sheaf is an isomorphism $\eta_{s,F}:F\xrightarrow{\sim}s_*s^{-1}F$, natural in $F$. For the constant commutative ring $\Lambda$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], clauses (1)--(3), identifies $s^{-1}\Lambda_U$ with $\Lambda_{U_{\mathrm{red}}}$ and identifies the module adjunction unit with this abelian unit. In particular $\eta_{s,F}$ is $\Lambda_U$-linear. Its inverse is linear as well: if $y=\eta_{s,F}(x)$ and $a$ is a local coefficient section, then $\eta_{s,F}^{-1}(ay)=\eta_{s,F}^{-1}(\eta_{s,F}(ax))=ax$. Hence it is an isomorphism of module sheaves. The reduction theorem and invariance theorem require neither a nilpotent bound on the nilradical nor any Noetherian or finiteness hypothesis.

proof.text: Put $G=s^{-1}F$. Let $d_{a,b}:(a\circ b)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}a_*b_*$ be the natural module direct-image composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], clause (1). Define the required map to be the composite $$j_*F\xrightarrow{\ j_*\eta_{s,F}\ }j_*s_*G\xrightarrow{\ d_{j,s,G}^{-1}\ }(j\circ s)_*G=(r\circ j_{\mathrm{red}})_*G\xrightarrow{\ d_{r,j_{\mathrm{red}},G}\ }r_*j_{\mathrm{red},*}G.$$ The middle equality uses step 1. The functor $j_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] sends the inverse of $\eta_{s,F}$ to an inverse of $j_*\eta_{s,F}$; the other arrows are module isomorphisms by the cited composition theorem. Thus the composite is a $\Lambda$-linear isomorphism. For a module morphism $a:F\to F\prime$, naturality of the unit gives $s_*s^{-1}(a)\circ\eta_{s,F}=\eta_{s,F\prime}\circ a$; apply $j_*$ and then the naturality squares for both $d$ comparisons to obtain $$r_*j_{\mathrm{red},*}s^{-1}(a)\circ\alpha_F=\alpha_{F\prime}\circ j_*(a),$$ where $\alpha_F$ is the displayed composite. This proves naturality in $F$ without an additional base-change theorem.
